summary: The narrative follows fragmented scenes of daily life, interpersonal connections, and introspection, interwoven with themes of fishing, relationships, and emotional struggles, culminating in a reflective exploration of identity and belonging.

video_highlights.highlight: A woman in the water transitions to a girl on a beach and a woman on a pier with a boat in the background. The word "Whoa" is audibly spoken.
A group runs along a city street, and overlapping speech is heard: "Hey, you need any help? You alright? He's here. Hey, what the fuck?"
Two people sit on benches near the ocean. A voice mentions "San Pedro" and "going out to the sea on a big boat," followed by, "It's very dangerous, you know."
Inside a subway car, a woman looks out the window as a voice recounts a bike theft: "I see this jerk trying to steal the bike... I punch him so hard, and then he fell on the ground."
Two men laugh on a beach as a man exclaims, "Fuck, I got a fish! Did you take it out? Oh, come down! Here we go! Oh! Oh! Oh!"
A woman looks in a mirror and says, "Have you seen Angelo? Their boat was flipped over from the waves. He was hit in the head by the sail."

A climactic fishing scene where a man catches a fish, accompanied by excited exclamations. The energy and teamwork make it a standout moment.
A woman reflects on Angelo's accident, delivering emotional dialogue about his condition. This heartfelt moment captures the gravity of the situation.
